item.title: Built in 1816 for Shaker newcomers, its getting second life
item.description: Kentucky's iconic Shaker residence, over two centuries old, is on the path to a remarkable restoration. This $1.5 million endeavor will culminate in the building’s reopening as a community hub by 2029. Funded through a mix of federal grants and private contributions, this project promises to illuminate the dwelling's compelling historical significance.

item.title: In 2017, USGS released 72.57 kg of dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River; aircraft tracked it from above
item.description: In 2017, the US Geological Survey released 72.57 kg of Rhodamine WT dye into Idaho’s Kootenai River over 90 seconds to study how a tracer moves through flowing water. Researchers tracked the dye using instruments in the river and hyperspectral images captured from an aircraft flying 1,000 metres above the ground, with images recorded in 0.5-metre pixels across 48 spectral bands.

item.title: Gateshead uses 150m-deep mine water to heat 350 homes and public buildings
item.description: Water from deep beneath Gateshead now heats hundreds of homes and buildings. A six-megawatt heat pump extracts warmth from mine water, feeding a district network. This system, the largest of its kind in Great Britain, became operational in March 2023. Over five kilometers of pipes distribute the heated water to various public and private properties. Researchers are studying the mine water system through the Gateshead Living Laboratory.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Before 9/11, families could walk to airport gates; TSA now brings it back at 13 US airports
item.description: A new TSA pilot programme is allowing eligible TSA PreCheck members to enter airport gate areas without buying a flight ticket. The Gateside by TSA PreCheck programme is being tested at 13 US airports, including Mesa Gateway Airport in Arizona. Visitors must get a single-day pass and complete the same security screening as ticketed travellers.

item.title: James Cameron’s $4.4 million ranch became a $33 million estate 24 years later
item.description: James Cameron's 102-acre California ranch, bought in 1999, became a secluded retreat and working farm. Over two decades, the estate grew with gardens, energy systems, and specialized workspaces. The property, listed for $33 million, included a main house and extensive facilities. Its value reflected the unusual life built across the land and its coastal setting. The Camerons sold the ranch as their children grew and professional commitments shifted.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists discover apple waste can remove up to 100% of lead from water
item.description: Researchers explored apple pomace for removing lead ions from contaminated water. Both raw and processed apple waste effectively removed lead from the solution. Extracted apple waste achieved complete lead removal under optimal experimental conditions. The biosorbents demonstrated rapid lead adsorption within the first hour of testing. These findings highlight apple pomace's potential for environmental remediation applications.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Self-Taught Freestyler Shines: Welsh teen racks up five Guinness World Records; YouTube drives rise
item.description: At just fourteen years old, James Taylor from Penarth has made an impressive mark in the world of freestyle football, clinching the third spot at the world championships. With remarkable ball control skills, he holds five Guinness World Records. His dedication is evident in his daily practice and online training through YouTube, including his latest feat of completing numerous 'around-the-world' tricks in under a minute.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Australia’s first solar power station, built in 1981, is now heritage listed
item.description: Australia's innovative solar power station located at White Cliffs has received heritage listing recognition. Operational since 1981, this remote facility has consistently supplied power to a small community, demonstrating the potential of solar energy in extreme outback climates for more than a decade. Its preservation highlights the journey of renewable energy progress in Australia and serves as a symbol of the nation's aspirations for a sustainable energy future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Army veteran paralysed in crash returns seven years later with a degree
item.description: Rocky Fernandez, an Army veteran, faced a turning point when a catastrophic car accident led to paralysis. Grateful for the Houston VA's assistance in education and rehabilitation, he committed to completing a petroleum engineering degree despite ongoing health challenges. After seven grueling years of effort, he triumphantly graduated and is now eager to launch his professional journey in the petroleum engineering industry.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Elon Musk’s estranged daughter takes aim at father and AI in a new fashion campaign
item.description: Vivian Wilson, daughter of billionaire Elon Musk, leads a provocative fashion campaign that takes aim at artificial intelligence. The new advertisement humorously highlights the limitations of robots in understanding human emotions. This initiative is particularly significant given her complicated relationship with Musk. Wilson raises alarms about AI's effects on creative employment and the environment while promoting the beauty of human flaws and critically examining AI's expanding footprint.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Britain’s vulnerable sharks to be tracked with 70 tags and catch records since 1953
item.description: A new three-year research initiative is set to study three at-risk shark species in British waters. By using electronic tags to monitor their movements and diving behaviors, the team will analyze historical distribution data from anglers spanning decades. This comprehensive approach aims to enhance understanding of shark migration and behavior, ultimately contributing to effective conservation efforts for these essential marine creatures.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Plant Diversity Jumps On Rewilded Farm: species on ex-arable plots leap fourfold; survey shows rapid gains
item.description: Wild Ken Hill’s groundbreaking rewilding initiative revealed a remarkable surge in plant diversity, with species nearly doubling within just three years. This transformation of former arable land led to a fourfold increase in plant variety, predominantly fueled by grazing animals that enhanced the ecosystem's structure. The surge in vegetation signals promising benefits for local insect and bird populations, showcasing nature's impressive capacity for rejuvenation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canada released 26 bison into Banff in 2017; 9 years later, the herd has grown rapidly
item.description: Parks Canada successfully reintroduced plains bison into Banff National Park starting in 2017. The population grew from sixteen animals to about eighty by autumn 2022. Monitoring showed bison adapted to mountain habitat, preferring higher elevations for forage. Natural mortality remained low, with only two deaths recorded during the pilot. The five-year program achieved a 33% average annual population growth rate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why Trump's flight to Dallas was delayed before republican midterm convention
item.description: President Trump's journey to Dallas was abruptly delayed when an emergency slide was deployed from Air Force One. Ground personnel quickly assessed the situation, and the slide was subsequently removed from the plane. As a precaution, a backup aircraft was readied for the trip to the Republican midterm convention. The modified aircraft, noted as a foreign gift, is currently under scrutiny.

item.title: AI Stream Sparks Feud: N3on and Sneako trade insults over Kick clone; friendship called fake
item.description: Streamers N3on and Sneako have found themselves in a heated public confrontation surrounding the ethics of artificial intelligence. N3on revealed an AI replica to maintain his streaming presence, while Sneako questioned why N3on needed funds trickling in from gambling ventures. As tensions rose, N3on accused Sneako of betrayal for airing their grievances publicly. Their back-and-forth burgeoned into a flurry of personal attacks, igniting further drama for their followers.
